statement_html:
How many complex numbers \(z\) there are such that \(z^{22}\)is equal to the conjugate of \(z\)?
Enter your reply:
=
solution_html: Let \(w\) be the conjugate of \(z\). We notice first that	\(z^{22}=w\) implies \(|z| = 1\) or 0. When \(|z| = 1\) we have \(w = \frac{1}{z}\),	therefore the complex numbers \(z\) verifying the condition of the problem are exactly the roots of the polynomial	\(X^{23} - 1\) or 0.
